title: The station phone called from my own number 📞
style_prompt: liminal empty office space, yellow wallpaper, damp beige carpet, buzzing fluorescent ceiling lights, one bright light source, well exposed, 35mm film grain, no people, no faces, no text, no watermark
hook_text: At 2:17 a.m. the inspection station phone rang.

scenes.narration: At 2:17 a.m. the inspection station phone rang. The caller ID was my own number.
I answered. Nobody spoke. Only an engine idling. And somewhere behind it, a pen scratching.
I looked at the bays. Bay two was lit. A car I had never seen was parked inside. Engine running. Nobody at the wheel.
I walked over. The windscreen was fogged from the inside. Someone had written on it with a finger. Just one word.
It said, behind. I did not turn around. I watched the glass instead. And in the reflection, I saw my lamp swaying.
The swinging lamp lit the floor under the car. The tyres were wet. Footprints, dry and dusty, led from the car to my counter.
I followed them. They stopped at my logbook. It was open. Tonight's page. One line.
It said, car inspected. Driver deceased. Inspector present. Signed, you.
The car door opened. The engine stopped. And I realised the phone was still ringing. In my pocket.
So tell me. Do you answer the phone, or close the door?
